summary.text: A 5-year-old boy with mucopolysaccharidosis type III underwent umbilical cord blood stem cell transplantation with graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis using methotrexate and cyclosporine A. No signs of graft-versus-host disease were observed, recovery progressed without difficulties apart from a little fever, and neutrophils were fully engrafted by day + 27.

Autoimmune hemolytic anemia manifested 144 days after transplantation with worsening anemia, nausea, vomiting and pallor. On admission he weighed 13.0 kg; hemoglobin was 26 g/L, reticulocytes 60.1 × 10^(9)/L, LDH 876 U/L, indirect bilirubin 53.3 μmol/L and ferritin 3630 pmol/L, with a positive direct anti-globulin test. Coombs-positive AIHA and cytomegalovirus were confirmed.

He received blood transfusions, plasma exchange, glucocorticoids, immunoglobulins and rituximab; during hospitalization this included 4 units of irradiated washed red blood cells and 30 g of immunoglobulin, with no notable enhancement in hemoglobin, bilirubin or LDH. Daratumumab was given, with variable hemolytic effects after the first 4 administrations, methylprednisolone in combination and transfusion if necessary; after the fifth injection on day + 211 he needed no transfusion for almost 1 week.

On day 276, at the fourth hospital visit, bilirubin, hemoglobin and LDH were within normal ranges, which the authors described as significant improvement after CD38 treatment. No adverse effects were noted. At telephone follow-up 546 days post-discharge, cognitive, language and other neurological functions were stable, with notable improvement in emotional and mental states.
